options: A system-generated, meaningless identifier that exists purely to identify a row
The identifier a row already had in the source system
A column that stores a calculated business metric
A key used only in OLTP systems, never in a warehouse
questions.explain: A surrogate key has no real-world meaning — it's typically a simple integer that SQL Server generates automatically, most often with IDENTITY.

questions.q: Which T-SQL column property is the easiest way to auto-generate a surrogate key?
options: IDENTITY
VARCHAR
DEFAULT NULL
UNIQUE INDEX only, with no other property
questions.explain: IDENTITY(seed, increment) tells SQL Server to assign each new row the next sequential integer automatically — the standard way to generate a surrogate key.

questions.q: Why does SCD Type 2 history specifically require a surrogate key rather than a natural key as the primary key?
options: A Type 2 change inserts a new row for the same real-world entity, which would violate uniqueness if the (repeating) natural key were the primary key
Natural keys are always too long to index
SCD Type 2 doesn't use keys at all
Surrogate keys are required by SQL Server syntax rules
questions.explain: Because the surrogate key — not the natural key — has to stay unique, the same natural key can appear on multiple surrogate-keyed rows, one per historical version.

questions.q: What is the conventional purpose of a surrogate key value of -1 in a dimension table?
options: Unknown — used when a lookup fails while loading a fact row
The most recently inserted row
The row with the highest sales total
A duplicate row that should be deleted
questions.explain: Reserved values like 0 (missing), -1 (unknown), -2 (N/A), and -3 (error) let a fact table's foreign key stay valid even when a real dimension match can't be found.

questions.q: What's the one common exception to keeping a surrogate key meaningless?
options: A date dimension's surrogate key is conventionally stored in a human-readable YYYYMMDD integer format
Product dimensions should always use the product's list price as the surrogate key
There are no exceptions — every surrogate key must be meaningless
Customer dimensions should use the customer's email address as the surrogate key
questions.explain: A YYYYMMDD-format integer surrogate key is standard practice for date dimensions specifically — it's readable, sorts correctly, and is the one accepted case for a meaningful surrogate key.
